future_argv:
Create one continuous five-second realistic live-action-looking synthetic shot of two fictional, non-identifying adult martial-arts performers. The initiator wears a deep navy training jacket and black training pants. The receiver wears a muted rust-orange training jacket and charcoal training pants. Both have ordinary realistic human faces and bodies, no resemblance to geometric mannequins, no branded clothing, and no identifying features.

Place them in a clean indoor training studio with a warm beige seamless wall and matte wooden floor. Use soft natural-looking studio illumination. There must be no props, grid, visible text, diagram, or calibration-stage appearance. Use a static three-quarter-front medium-wide camera at approximately chest height. Keep both complete bodies and both sets of feet visible with generous margins throughout. Use a stable 16:9 composition with no camera movement, zoom, shake, or crop change, and do not recreate a pure reference side view.

Use the supplied video only as a motion reference for the full-duration temporal and body-mechanics sequence: preparation, approach, one contact episode, post-contact result, release or retraction, recovery, non-contact repositioning, and active ending. The reference must not control identity, face, body appearance, mannequin design, colors, clothing, scene, background, camera angle, framing, lighting, props, text, story, or visual style. Do not copy any contact marker, ring, flash, arrow, grid, joint node, calibration-stage cue, color palette, or reference composition.

Action family: push reaction. At 0.0-0.6 seconds, begin with both performers clearly separated while they make small guard and weight-preparation movements. At 0.6-1.2 seconds, the initiator approaches while the receiver braces without retreating or making contact. At 1.2-1.5 seconds, the initiator performs one short two-hand torso push with one clearly readable contact episode. The receiver must not react before contact. At 1.4-2.1 seconds, the receiver shows readable torso displacement caused by the push and makes exactly one rear-foot recovery placement, with no second retreat step. At 1.5-2.3 seconds, the initiator releases pressure and retracts both arms promptly. At 2.3-3.2 seconds, both restore balance and guard. At 3.2-4.1 seconds, both perform controlled non-contact repositioning and weight redistribution. At 4.1-5.0 seconds, both continue a small non-contact guard response, torso adjustment, balance movement, and natural breathing through the final frame. There must be exactly one contact episode and exactly one receiver rear-foot recovery result.

There must be no second contact, multi-step retreat, falling, frame escape, prolonged contact, sustained pressure, extended-arm freeze, or long static tail. Both performers must remain fully visible and continue small natural guard, balance, torso, and breathing movement through the final frame. This text controls identity, clothing, scene, camera, composition, lighting, and visual style; the supplied video controls motion only.
